title: Continuous telemetry can enable linkage of sessions and identities
description: The wearable receives a persistent stream of heart rate, step counts, GPS position, and timestamps from the wearer. Even if explicit identifiers are absent, the combination of location traces, temporal patterns, and physiological telemetry can allow records from different sessions to be linked to the same individual and potentially linked with external datasets.
assumptions: Assumes the device or downstream system stores or processes telemetry with sufficient persistence to correlate repeated observations over time.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is based on best judgement because the retrieved context only gives applicable threat types, not detailed node ids.

title: Sensor telemetry may identify the wearer
description: GPS position histories, timestamps, activity patterns, and heart-rate characteristics can directly or indirectly identify the wearer. Home/work locations and routine movement patterns are especially identifying, making this flow privacy-sensitive even without a name attached.
assumptions: Assumes telemetry is retained or observable in a form that preserves fine-grained location and timing data.
uncertainty_note: Detailed threat-tree node id is approximate; identification clearly applies to this flow.

title: The flow reveals sensitive personal information
description: Continuous capture of heart rate, step counts, GPS position, and timestamps discloses health, behavior, routines, whereabouts, and potentially special-category personal data. This can reveal exercise habits, sleep/wake cycles, visits to sensitive locations, and other intimate aspects of the wearer's life.
assumptions: Assumes the telemetry is accessible to the device software and possibly stored or transmitted onward.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is approximate; disclosure is strongly supported by the nature of the data.

title: Continuous sensing may occur without sufficient user awareness
description: Because the device is worn continuously, the wearer may not remain adequately aware of the extent, frequency, granularity, or persistence of telemetry collection. Background capture of GPS and physiological data can therefore create a detectability issue: sensitive processing may be hard for the user to notice at the moment it occurs.
assumptions: Assumes the device does not provide persistent, clear, and timely indicators of active sensing and data capture.
uncertainty_note: Applicability depends on the actual user interface and indicators provided by the wearable.

title: Collection purpose and downstream use may be unclear to the wearer
description: From this flow alone, the wearer may not understand which sensors are active continuously, for what purposes telemetry is collected, how long it is retained, or with whom it will be shared. This creates a risk that processing is insufficiently transparent and therefore users cannot form an accurate mental model of system behavior.
assumptions: Assumes notices, onboarding, or just-in-time explanations are incomplete or not salient during continuous collection.
uncertainty_note: This is a plausible threat for continuous wearable sensing, but actual applicability depends on the product's transparency mechanisms.

title: Continuous collection may exceed necessity or valid consent expectations
description: Always-on capture of heart rate, steps, GPS position, and timestamps may process more personal data than is necessary for a specific function, or may rely on consent that is not sufficiently specific, informed, or revocable. Fine-grained location and physiological telemetry are particularly sensitive and may require stronger justification and controls.
assumptions: Assumes not every listed data type is strictly necessary for the intended service at all times, or that consent/other legal basis is not granular enough.
uncertainty_note: Non-compliance depends on jurisdiction, purpose limitation, data minimization choices, and consent design; threat is grounded in the breadth and sensitivity of the flow.

title: Excessive disclosure of precise activity and location data during sync
description: The wearable-to-app sync transfers exercise sessions, GPS traces, device identifier, and timestamps. This is highly sensitive personal data, and the full batch may exceed what is strictly necessary for the companion app's immediate function. Precise GPS traces combined with timestamps can reveal home/work locations, routines, and sensitive visits; the device identifier enables persistent association across syncs.
assumptions: Assumes the companion app does not strictly need full-resolution GPS traces, persistent device identifiers, or complete historical batches for every sync, and that data minimization has not yet been demonstrated.

title: Stable device identifier and repeated sync metadata enable identifiability
description: Including a device id in each sync can make the data directly or indirectly identifiable to the companion app, especially when combined with timestamps, exercise patterns, and GPS traces. Even if user account data is handled elsewhere, this flow alone may allow singling out and persistent recognition of the same individual/device over time.
assumptions: Assumes the device id is stable across sessions and accessible to the app in a form that supports correlation.
